There is no native support (yet) for time series in Rattle.

> I import the data and run the Predictive. But where do I put in the data for
> today so I can get a prediction for tomorrow? For example: Rain or Not rain.

Thanks for the question. I've released 2.5.24 - the Evaluate tab now
has a "Enter" data option. Selecting the Score option, and this new
"Enter" option will pop up the R data frame editor to allow you to
enter data yourself, and then have Rattle score it. So you can enter
today's value for the variables and then Rattle will predict rain or
not rain for tomrrow.

Version 2.5.24 is currently propagating through CRAN.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Memory problems in R...
parts:
Your "3+ GB RAM" is not very much. And Linux does not provide memory that is not installed. 3GB in Linux will be the same 3GB that you have with Windows. The R for Windows FAQ has information about how to maximize your memory efficiency. Going to UNIX or Linux will not help and may even hurt since the 64 bit pointers actually consume more memory so if you have less than 4 GB of RAM you may not see much improvement. So unless you are willing to invest in larger amounts of memory at the same time as you switch to an OS with a 64 bit memory manager , you will need to develop some workarounds like sampling.

-- 
David.
